title: Galvanize Integrations & Runtime Handoff
summary: Kickoff for implementation runway and technical handoff: reviewed VPC networking, access patterns, primary success criteria (latency < 120ms p95 for chat, batch embeddings cost target), security needs (KMS, audit logs, SOC2 questions), staging pilot plan and benchmarking approach.
topics: VPC peering and private deployment options
KMS/HSM and data encryption at rest
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-24 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood CSM), Priya (Galvanize CTO), Marcos (DevOps), Elaine (Security), Tom (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Quick technical intake + network handoff
- Agreed pilot scope: 2 models, staging env, set of 5 eval prompts
- Action items: VPC details, SSO metadata, benchmark spreadsheet link

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um i'll kick us off, we planned 45ish minutes, a quick intro and then jonah will walk through the runtime and then we'll cover security and the pilot plan
[01:12] Priya (Galvanize): thanks maya, quick intros from our side — i'm priya, cto, marcos is devops, elaine handles security, tom is pm on this integration
[02:05] Jonah (Redwood SE): cool, i'm jonah — i'll focus on infra and routing, think of this as the handoff from onboarding into implementation. i'll call out the things that typically block customers early: peering, egress rules, kms perms, and model quant profiles
[03:30] Marcos (Galvanize): yeah — on peering we prefer VPC peering for now, no shared services allowed, we need ip ranges and firewall rules from redwood to open
[04:05] Maya (Redwood): totally — we'll share a template. quick note: for private customers we support both VPC peering and private link, and there's an onprem bundle if you need airgapped later
[05:20] Elaine (Galvanize): on encryption, are you using customer-managed keys or do you manage KMS? we need HSM-backed keys for PHI scope
[06:05] Jonah (Redwood SE): good question — for Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM; we also offer integration with common cloud KMS. there's an HSM workflow for key import. i'll send the kms onboarding doc link afterwards (link: https://redwood.example/docs/kms-quickstart)
[07:30] Tom (Galvanize): pilot success metrics — priya mentioned p95 latency target and cost threshold, can we capture those now?
[08:00] Priya (Galvanize): target is sub-120ms p95 for simple chat flows and under $0.002 per embedding equivalent, roughly. if we can't hit that in hosted mode we'll consider dedicated nodes
[09:15] Jonah (Redwood SE): noted. a lot will depend on sequence length and batching. we'll run the first benchmark in staging with realistic token distributions. small caveat: quantization improves cost but may slightly alter outputs — we'll include quality checks in evals
[11:00] Maya (Redwood): ok team — security checklist items: soc2 attestation, audit log retention, sso metadata. elaine, do you need an SOC2 report up front?
[11:32] Elaine (Galvanize): yes, SOC2 and also an encryption attestation. also full audit logs for model access tied to user id's, and we need to map RBAC to our groups
[12:20] Jonah (Redwood SE): we can export audit logs to your S3, and we support SAML SSO. mapping roles usually goes: rd-owner -> admin, devops -> infra, engineer -> read/write. we'll share a sample SAML metadata and an RBAC mapping doc
[14:05] Marcos (Galvanize): on networking specifics, can you confirm egress ip ranges? our firewall team wants to pin them down
[15:10] Jonah (Redwood SE): yes — staging and prod have different ranges, i'll include both. also note: when using Dedicated capacity we can NAT through your VPC to avoid wide egress ACLs
[17:00] Priya (Galvanize): curious on model variants — how do rollbacks and canary deploys work? if a new quantized variant regresses do we have automatic fallback?
[17:45] Jonah (Redwood SE): yes we have rollout policies: canary percent, health checks (latency/error), and automatic fallback to previous model variant or hosted baseline. that lives in the console under rollouts -> policies. some transcription note: the system earlier spelled 'rollout' as 'role out' in notes, ignore that
[19:30] Tom (Galvanize): for the pilot, what telemetry do we get? token-level cost, p95, tail latency?
[20:10] Ravi (Redwood CSM): yep, console exposes token cost breakdown, per-route latency, and traces. we can also ship a daily csv to your analytics bucket if preferred
[21:40] Elaine (Galvanize): does redwood keep training data or logs that could contain PHI? we need a guarantee of not retaining input/output beyond X days
[22:10] Maya (Redwood): by default hosted calls are retained for 30 days for quality/ops but for private/dedicated we can disable retention; we'll document retention SLA. i'll flag this as high priority
[24:00] Jonah (Redwood SE): demo of runtime topology (verbal): requests hit the gateway -> auth layer -> router (policy-based) -> serving runtime. runtime does continuous batching and uses kv-cache for prefix reuse. note: transcript sometimes converted 'KV cache' to 'K V cash' — apologies
[26:45] Priya (Galvanize): can we run a baseline benchmark against your verified model profile so we have apples-to-apples?
[27:20] Jonah (Redwood SE): yes, we publish model profiles with throughput/latency for sequence lengths. we'll run a 48-hour benchmark in staging. i'd like your devs to provide a representative prompt set and token histogram
[29:10] Marcos (Galvanize): we'll send a sample of top 100 prompts and a typical token length CSV by monday
[30:00] Maya (Redwood): perfect. on timeline, pilot -> 2 weeks of benchmarking and evals -> canary for 1 week -> full prod. does that feel reasonable?
[30:45] Priya (Galvanize): timeline okay but we need security review signoff before canary. elaine will own that
[31:15] Elaine (Galvanize): yes i'll do review, need SOC2 artifacts and KMS flow + runbook for incident response
[33:40] Tom (Galvanize): question about cost controls — can we set per-route budget caps and alerts?
[34:05] Ravi (Redwood CSM): yes, per-route quotas, rate limits, and cost alerts. we'll set an initial daily cap for the pilot and notify your billing contact when thresholds hit 70/90%
[35:50] Priya (Galvanize): any competitors or alternatives we should be aware of in feature gaps? our infra team asked about model privacy guarantees vs Anthropic and some onprem vendors
[36:30] Maya (Redwood): noted — competitors mentioned in past deals include Anthropic (privacy features), BigCloud AI (easy managed endpoints) and a few onprem inference vendors. we'll share a short comparison doc
[37:50] Jonah (Redwood SE): operational notes: for embedding workloads use batching window of 50ms, that typically hits throughput targets; for chat keep window small to preserve latency. quant profiles we recommend: 4-bit for embeddings, 8-bit for chat initial tests
[39:10] Marcos (Galvanize): ok we'll start with hosted staging to speed visibility then lock down private if needed after benchmarks
[40:45] Maya (Redwood): recap before we close: redwood to send VPC template, SAML metadata, KMS onboarding doc, benchmark spreadsheet + model profile links. galv to send prompt set, firewall CIDRs, and SOC2 contact
[42:00] Priya (Galvanize): sounds good. one more: do you have a runbook for incidents when model hallucinations trigger PII exposure?
[42:32] Jonah (Redwood SE): yes — incident runbook exists, includes immediate model rollback, blacklist triggers, and data purge steps. i'll attach runbook link in follow up
[44:15] Tom (Galvanize): ok next step for tom/pm is to schedule a 1-hour tech deep-dive once you share the staging credentials
[45:00] Maya (Redwood): great, thanks all. we'll follow up with docs and set the deep-dive. thanks elaine for the security constraints callout.
[47:10] Priya (Galvanize): thanks everyone, bye
[47:30] Meeting end
